newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits quietky steady ahead of CPI.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits quietky steady ahead of CPI.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were quietly steady in lacklustre trade, dealers said on Wednesday.
They said most traders were sidelined ahead of tonight's release of the U.S January consumer price index, which is forecast to be unchanged from December's 0.3 percent increase.

"Rates were steady to higher in the morning on some position adjustments. All eyes are on tonight's release of the (U.S. January) consumer price index, but unless the numbers are way off market expectations, I don't think there will be much impact," a local dealer said.
"Some people are also waiting for fresh clues to market direction from Thursday's issue of the weekly jobless claims and housing starts figures," he said.
In day-to-day rates, Wednesday/Thursday and Thursday/Friday rose 1/16 percentage point each to a common 5-3/8 5-1/4 percent, respectively. Week-fixed was unchanged from Tuesday's 5-3/8 5-1/4 percent.

Among longer dates, one-month was unchanged from Tuesday's 5-3/8 5-1/4 percent, three-months unchanged at 5-1/2 5-3/8, nine-months unchanged at 5-5/8 5-1/2 and twelve-months unchanged at 5-3/4 5-5/8 percent. - P. Theseira (65-870-3085)
